subject: Discrepancies in Results Between Old and New GGIR Versions

messages.author: cb76670240837e52
messages.subject: Discrepancies in Results Between Old and New GGIR Versions
parts:
Hi,
I am a little confused of results of the same individual in two different version of GGIR. We aimed to calculate the Sleep Regularity Index (SRI) using the "sleepreg" function, which is compatible only with GGIR version 2.0.0, not the latest version. To proceed, I had to remove the latest GGIR version from my laptop and reinstall version 2.0.0. However, I'm encountering issues with the results in this version: individuals from time zones other than EST (such as PST and Mountain Standard) show significantly different outcomes in the older GGIR version compared to the latest. It appears that the results from GGIR 2.0.0 may not be accurate, though I'm uncertain about the cause of this discrepancy between the two versions.
I've attached my R code, as well as a presentation comparing actigraphy double plots, sleep onset, wake times, and sleep duration across both versions to highlight these differences. Additionally, I've noticed that some summary report files generated are 0-byte files with no data output.
One more question: the "sleepreg" function uses files from the ms3.out folder within GGIR, but it sometimes encounters 0 or negative values, preventing SRI calculation. 
This results in the following error: "simpleError in onoffvector_cons_miscl[NAon] <- NA: only 0's may be mixed with negative subscripts." Could you advise on resolving this error?

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Discrepancies in Results Between Old and New GGIR Versions
parts:
Dear Arpita,

GGIR release 2.0-0 was from May 2020, Sleep Regularity Index (SRI) was added to GGIR in release 2.4-3 in 2021 as you can see in the GGIR change log.

There is no 'sleepreg' function in GGIR, and I suppose you are using https://github.com/dpwindred/sleepreg and that this is actually an error in their software? Note that it has been a very peculiar effort by them to develop complementary functionality to GGIR without communicating about it with me as GGIR maintainer. By the time they had published their work I had implemented SRI inside GGIR rendering their secret effort a complete waste of time. If you have issues with their code please contact them. However, I would recommend using the sleep regularity index as implemented in GGIR, which is also much better able to handle missing data.

Release 2.0-0 is known to have major bugs as I have communicated with collaborates and with co-authors (Lane, Weedon etc) of the Windred paper in 2021. The fact that they kept on using 2.0-0 has been their decision. For me reflections on why GGIR has changed between version, see also my response in this thread.

If you have specific suggestions about inaccuracies or bugs in the latest GGIR version then I look forward to your report.

Thanks,

Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/
